title: A million open connections and a deploy
summary: Real-time chat reaches a million concurrent connections. Then a deploy drops all of them at once.

statement.situation: A real-time messaging product keeps one long-lived connection per active user. New connections arrive at about 8,000 per second and last around two minutes, so the fleet settles at close to a million simultaneous connections. Each gateway machine has a fixed amount of memory and can only complete so many new TLS handshakes per second. Every release restarts the gateways and drops every connection at once.
symptoms: During a deploy the gateways report a surge of connection attempts many times their normal rate
Handshake capacity is saturated; most attempts fail and clients retry immediately
It takes minutes for the fleet to settle, and some gateways run out of memory
requirements: Hold roughly a million connections with memory headroom (under 90% full)
A deploy must not cause a reconnect storm (no more than 5,000 refused connection attempts per second)
constraints: Gateway machine size, memory per connection and handshake rate are fixed
You can change how many gateways run and how clients behave when disconnected

learningObjectives: Connection capacity from memory and per-node limits
Sizing for failure and deploys, not just steady state

references.title: Phoenix: the road to 2 million websocket connections

scenarios.name: Steady state, then a deploy at t=420 s
scenarios.description: 8,000 new connections/s. At t=420 s every gateway restarts and all connections drop.

successCriteria.label: Refused connection attempts stay ≤ 5,000/s through the deploy
